sections.title: Intake
sections.conclusion: Baseline fields and source anchors establish whether the proposal can be reviewed at all.

sections.title: Claims and evidence
findings: Proposal document read by reasoning layer: yes

Requested: A 12-month Governance Incentives Framework project covering research, governance data collection, incentive modeling, dashboarding, community engagement, a controlled pilot, a CIP, and a governance integration pathway.

Deliverables: Governance Incentives Framework report, public governance activity dataset, public website and dashboard, documented incentive models and formula outputs, controlled incentive pilot findings report, at least one publication-ready research paper submitted for peer review, completed and submitted Governance Incentives Framework CIP, governance integration pathway and handover documentation, final financial and milestone report

Claim (governance, proposer_asserted, high materiality): The proposal says Cardano lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, high materiality): The proposal cites early governance data showing active DReps declined in every 12-epoch period, DRep Gini increased from 0.92 to 0.94, and 11-16 DReps represent 51% of voting power.

Claim (governance, independently_verifiable, medium materiality): The Governance Incentives Working Group has created a mapping document identifying 49 relevant efforts, proposals, research papers, tools, and related initiatives in the governance incentives space.

Claim (technical, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will deliver seven staged milestones over 12 months from discovery through final reporting, CIP submission, and governance integration planning.

Claim (governance, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The project will evaluate incentive mechanisms for participation, decentralization, concentration risk, accountability, gaming risk, shallow compliance behavior, and budget sustainability.

Claim (economic, supported_in_proposal, high materiality): The proposal requests a total budget of ₳4,207,967 allocated across conceptualization, community engagement, modeling, data engineering, dashboarding, administration, research, pilot costs, additional costs, contingency, and independent audit and oversight.
missing: Independent evidence for: The proposal says Cardano lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time.
Independent evidence for: The named team members and contributor claim prior Cardano governance, Catalyst, research, teaching, consulting, and delivery experience.

Independent evidence for: The proposal claims the framework will reduce uncertainty before Cardano adopts permanent governance incentive mechanisms that could distribute substantial treasury funds for many years.
sections.conclusion: Each claim must map to replayable public evidence; proposer assertions alone are not enough for confidence.

sections.title: Treasury analysis
findings: Six-month treasury flow regime: unknown (stale snapshot) (basis: total inflow (tau + donations) vs enacted withdrawals)
sections.conclusion: Treasury votes require a higher bar because they consume shared ADA and create precedent.

sections.title: Risk review
sections.conclusion: Risk is not a side note; unmitigated execution or governance risk can dominate an otherwise attractive proposal.

sections.title: Counterargument pass
findings: Strongest YES: the proposal substantiates "The proposal cites early governance data showing active DReps declined in every 12-epoch period, DRep Gini increased from 0.92 to 0.94, and 11-16 DReps represent 51% of voting power." and clears the evidence gates.

Strongest NO: a material claim is unsupported — "The proposal says Cardano lacks a structured, data-driven framework for determining how governance contributions should be incentivized, measured, or supported over time." — so cost or precedent may outweigh the benefit.
Strongest hold: if claims cannot be tied to replayable evidence, abstaining avoids overclaiming certainty.
sections.conclusion: A defensible rationale must show the best opposing case before it reaches a vote.

sections.title: Synthesis
findings: Final vote must be derived from completed sections above, not from a prose summary.
The public rationale should name the decisive section and the strongest counterargument.
sections.conclusion: The vote is only credible if the assessment tree shows enough work for a skeptical delegator to audit.
